title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and increase throughput for common decoding workloads by upgrading the attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 variants, adding fused rotary/ROPE ops, and integrating KV-aware continuous batching and scheduler heuristics. This PR introduces a runtime switch to prefer fused kernels when the model/sequence length and device support them, adds rotary/rope fusion to avoid extra transpose/reshape overhead, and plumbs KV-batching hints through the scheduler so requests with warm KV caches are grouped for lower per-token overhead. Changes include kernel updates, scheduling heuristics, compatibility fallbacks, unit and perf tests, and documentation. Checklist: - [x] Implement FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused op paths - [x] Add fused rotary/ROPE kernels and tests - [x] Integrate KV-batching hints into scheduler and continuous-batching loop - [x] Add runtime feature flag and model-compatibility checks - [x] Add microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf test harness - [x] Update docs and CHANGELOG. Performance summary: 1) Up to 1.25x throughput improvement on A100 for medium-length sequences (512-1024) in steady-state; 2) Mean p95 latency reduced by ~18% for chat-like workloads with warm KV cache; 3) End-to-end token cost reduced ~20% in internal benchmarks when batching and fused ops are enabled. Compatibility/fallbacks: the runtime falls back to previous attention path when device or model shape is unsupported; an env var REDWOOD_USE_FUSED_ATTN can force enable/disable for testing. Related Linear items: ENG-7821 (attn kernel upgrade), ENG-8002 (scheduler kv-batching integration).

release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE ops; default runtime will prefer fused kernels when supported.
Scheduler now propagates KV-batching hints to continuous batching, improving throughput for workloads with warm KV caches.
Performance: up to 25% throughput improvement and ~18% p95 latency reduction in typical decoding workloads (see internal benchmark results).
Fallback to legacy attention path when device/model unsupported. Configurable with REDWOOD_USE_FUSED_ATTN.
